63923-the-old-red-sandstone-or-new-walks.title: New Walks In An Old Field.
63923-the-old-red-sandstone-or-new-walks.creator: Unknown
63923-the-old-red-sandstone-or-new-walks.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Smith, the father of English Geology, loved to remark that he had been born upon the Oolite--the formation whose various deposits he was the first to distinguish and describe, and from which, as from the meridian line of the geographer, the geological scale has been graduated on both sides.

9616-ramuntcho.title: Ramuntcho
9616-ramuntcho.creator: Pierre Loti
9616-ramuntcho.description: A book by Pierre Loti. But the autumn, when it comes to put an end to the plants, brings only a sort of far-off warning to man, a little more durable, who resists several winters and lets himself be lured several times by the charm of spring.

arxiv-2103-04697.title: A Review of Spatiotemporal Models for Count Data in R Packages. A Case Study of COVID-19 Data
arxiv-2103-04697.creator: María Victoria Ibañez, Marina Martínez-Garcia, Amelia Simó
arxiv-2103-04697.description: Abstract Spatio-temporal models for count data are required in a wide range of scientific fields and they have become particularly crucial nowadays because of their ability to analyse COVID-19-related data. Models for count data are needed when the variable of interest take only non-negative integer values and these integers arise from counting occurrences.

arxiv-2208-00925.title: Cluster Statistics in Expansive Combinatorial Structures
arxiv-2208-00925.creator: Konstantinos Panagiotou, Leon Ramzews
arxiv-2208-00925.description: Abstract We develop a simple and unified approach to investigate several aspects of the cluster statistics of random expansive (multi-)sets. In particular, we determine the limiting distribution of the size of the smallest and largest clusters, we establish all moments of the distribution of the number of clusters, and we prove a local limit theorem for that distribution.

arxiv-2303-12050.title: CurveCloudNet: Processing Point Clouds with 1D Structure
arxiv-2303-12050.creator: Colton Stearns, Davis Rempe, Alex Fu, Jiateng Liu, Sébastien Mascha, Jeong Joon Park, Despoina Paschalidou, Leonidas J. Guibas
arxiv-2303-12050.description: Abstract Modern depth sensors such as LiDAR operate by sweeping laser-beams across the scene, resulting in a point cloud with notable 1D curve-like structures. In this work, we introduce a new point cloud processing scheme and backbone, called CurveCloudNet, which takes advantage of the curve-like structure inherent to these sensors.

arxiv-2503-02444.title: Resonance for life: Metabolism and Social Interactions in Bacterial Communities
arxiv-2503-02444.creator: Eleonora Alfinito a , Matteo Beccaria a,b,c
arxiv-2503-02444.description: Abstract The social organization of microorganisms has long been a fascinating and challenging subject in both biology and sociology. In these organisms, the role of the individual is far less dominant than that of the community, which functions as a superorganism. The coordination is achieved through a communication mechanism known as quorum sensing.

pmc-10609522.title: How Does CBG Administration Affect Sphingolipid Deposition in the Liver of Insulin-Resistant Rats?
pmc-10609522.creator: Wiktor Bzdęga, Piotr Franciszek Kurzyna, Ewa Harasim-Symbor, Adam Hołownia, Adrian Chabowski, Karolina Konstantynowicz-Nowicka
pmc-10609522.description: Background: Cannabigerol (CBG), a non-psychotropic phytocannabinoid found in Cannabis sativa plants, has been the focus of recent studies due to its potential therapeutic properties. We proposed that by focusing on sphingolipid metabolism, which plays a critical role in insulin signaling and the development of insulin resistance, CBG may provide a novel therapeutic approach for metabolic disorders, particularly insulin resistance.

pmc-10669403.title: Brittle Asthma: Still on Board?
pmc-10669403.creator: Dina Visca, Francesco Ardesi, Rosella Centis, Patrizia Pignatti, Antonio Spanevello
pmc-10669403.description: (1) Background: “Brittle Asthma” was considered an asthma clinical phenotype and deemed to be life-threatening in the early 2000s; then, this definition disappeared. The purpose of this review is to examine what has historically been referred to as this term and see whether it may be applied to modern clinical practice, thus acquiring fresh relevance and meaning.

pmc-11405947.title: Atypical Cardiac Anatomy Leading to Subvalvar Aortic Stenosis in a 19-Month-Old Boy With a Murmur
pmc-11405947.creator: Elise A Stave, Yves d’Udekem, Amanda del Rosario, Sofia S Hanabergh, Sam P Gulino, Craig A Sable
pmc-11405947.description: A 19-month-old boy presented with a murmur and was found to have an unusual etiology of subvalvar aortic stenosis with discrete subaortic membrane and anomalous attachment of the anterior mitral valve papillary muscle to the interventricular septum. Preoperative suspicion for mitral valve involvement impacted surgical planning.

pmc-11500402.title: PNIPAM Mesoglobules in Dependence on Pressure
pmc-11500402.creator: Bart-Jan Niebuur, Vitaliy Pipich, Marie-Sousai Appavou, Dharani Mullapudi, Alec Nieth, Eric Rende, Alfons Schulte, Christine M. Papadakis
pmc-11500402.description: Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) in aqueous solution forms mesoglobules above its cloud point temperature Tcp. While these are small and compact at atmospheric pressure, they are large and water-rich at high pressure. To identify the transition between these states, we employed optical microscopy and carried out isothermal pressure scans.

pmc-11624193.title: Coupling cellular drug-target engagement to downstream pharmacology with CeTEAM
pmc-11624193.creator: Nicholas C K Valerie, Kumar Sanjiv, Oliver Mortusewicz, Si Min Zhang, Seher Alam, Maria J Pires, Hannah Stigsdotter, Azita Rasti, Marie-France Langelier, Daniel Rehling, Adam Throup, Oryn Purewal-Sidhu, Matthieu Desroses, Jacob Onireti, Prasad Wakchaure, Ingrid Almlöf, Johan Boström, Luka Bevc, Gior
pmc-11624193.description: Cellular target engagement technologies enable quantification of intracellular drug binding; however, simultaneous assessment of drug-associated phenotypes has proven challenging. Here, we present cellular target engagement by accumulation of mutant as a platform that can concomitantly evaluate drug-target interactions and phenotypic responses using conditionally stabilized drug biosensors. We observe that drug-responsive proteotypes are prevalent among reported mutants of known drug targets.

pmc-12290535.title: Alpha-band fluctuations represent behaviorally relevant excitability changes as a consequence of top–down guided spatial attention in a probabilistic spatial cueing design
pmc-12290535.creator: Christopher Gundlach, Norman Forschack, Matthias M Müller
pmc-12290535.description: Spatial attention is a key function enabling the selection of relevantinformation and meaningful behavioral responses and is likely implemented bydifferent neural mechanisms. In previous work, attention led to robust butuncorrelated modulations of Steady-State-Visual-Evoked-Potentials (SSVEPs) as amarker of early sensory gain and visual as well as motor alpha-band activity. Weprobed the behavioral relevance of attention-modulated trial-by-trialfluctuations of these measures.

pmc-12425865.title: The role of the transcription factor PATZ1 in tumorigenesis and metabolic regulation
pmc-12425865.creator: Yin Zheng, Jiabo Chen, Cheng Su
pmc-12425865.description: PATZ1 (POZ/BTB and AT hook containing zinc finger 1) is an important member of the POZ/BTB (Poxvirus and Zinc finger / Broad-complex, Tramtrack, and Bric-à-brac) family and has been confirmed to be involved in the development and progression of various tumors. Moreover, differential expression of PATZ1 is associated with the prognosis of multiple cancers and systemic metabolic patterns.

pmc-12540166.title: Genetic reinstatement of RIG-I in chickens reveals insights into avian immune evolution and influenza interaction
pmc-12540166.creator: Hicham Sid, Theresa von Heyl, Sabrina Schleibinger, Romina Klinger, Leah Heymelot Nabel, Hanna Vikkula, Rodrigo Guabiraba, Vanaique Guillory, Ryan Scicluna, Mohanned Naif Alhussien, Brigitte Böhm, Benjamin Schade, Daniel Elleder, Samantha Sives, Lonneke Vervelde, Sascha Trapp, Benjamin Schusser
pmc-12540166.description: Retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) activates mitochondrial antiviral signaling proteins, initiating the antiviral response. RIG-I and RNF135, a ubiquitin ligase regulator, are missing in domestic chickens but conserved in mallard ducks. The chickens’ RIG-I loss was long believed to be linked to increased avian influenza susceptibility.

pmc-12603694.title: Association of the triglyceride–glucose index with all-cause and cause-specific mortality in patients with comorbid hypertension and diabetes: A population-based cohort study
pmc-12603694.creator: Jiahao Zou, Song Lu, Kaishen Cao, Ruihong He, Xia Feng, Shuang Yang, Wen Liu, Haochen Liu, Zhichao Wang, Ruichun Liao, Jin Chen, Xiaoting Jiang, Xiaoping Peng
pmc-12603694.description: Study objectiveAlthough the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index has been shown to be an independent risk factor for either hypertension or diabetes, its association with the coexistence of both conditions remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TyG index and all-cause and cause-specific mortality among patients with comorbid hypertension and diabetes.

pmc-12665324.title: A comprehensive review of summer mortality syndrome in fish: Causes, climate impact, and mitigation strategies
pmc-12665324.creator: Manal E Shafi
pmc-12665324.description: Global warming poses a significant threat to aquatic animals, particularly fish production, because of the rising summer temperatures, leading to issues such as summer mortality syndrome. This issue could impact fish farms, leading to 30%–100% mortality rates and significant financial losses.

pmc-12834474.title: KIF18A promotes chromosome congression in cooperation with CENP-E downstream of CENP-C
pmc-12834474.creator: Jiahang Miao, Masatoshi Hara, Kuan-Chung Su, Heather R. Keys, Weixia Kong, Yusuke Takenoshita, Iain M. Cheeseman, Tatsuo Fukagawa
pmc-12834474.description: SUMMARYChromosome congression is a key process that acts to align chromosomes at the spindle equator via kinetochore-microtubule interactions, with defects in chromosome alignment leading to chromosomal instability. However, defining the mechanisms that underlie chromosome congression is limited due to the multiple factors that act in parallel to regulate chromosome movement.

pmc-13296648.title: Integrated Immune–Gut Profiling Identifies an Exploratory Pediatric Inflammatory Intestinal Profile Associated with Food-Specific IgG Reactivity
pmc-13296648.creator: Laura-Mihaela Ion, Carmen Pavelescu, Denisa Maria Canut, Mihaela Oros, Gheorghita Jugulete, Smaranda Diaconescu

pmc-13567519.title: The Rhizosphere Microbiome: A Key Mediator of Crop Responses to Fertilization Strategies
pmc-13567519.creator: Zhihui Zhao, Qihua Wu, Zerong Sun, Wenling Zhou, Junhua Ao
pmc-13567519.description: The rhizosphere microbiome, the plant’s “second genome” is pivotal for crop nutrient acquisition, health, and stress responses. While fertilization ensures high agricultural yields, a key challenge is reshaping this microbiome to boost crop performance. This review synthesizes how mineral, organic, and bio-organic/microbial inoculant fertilizers affect rhizosphere microbial structure, diversity, and function.
